modelFailoverTruth.whatWasWrong: routeModel has ranked `alternatives` since it was written and nothing ever executed down them. A grep for failover/fallbackProvider/FALLBACK across src/ returned no files: a quota wall failed the run next to a list naming which model should have served it.

modules.src/agent-model-failover.mjs: walks the order; never ranks, never calls a provider itself
modules.src/agent-model-routing-integration.mjs: failoverOrder binds ranked alternatives back to already-authorized workers
modules.src/agent-worker-runtime.mjs: deferTerminalSubmission, so exactly one outcome reaches the relay
modules.src/agent-worker-job.mjs: runAgentWorkerTick walks the chain; only the ending attempt submits

modelFailoverTruth.provenBy: tests/agent-model-failover.test.mjs, 22 tests covering all eleven required scenarios plus six more; mutations ROUTE-02..ROUTE-06 all killed
modelFailoverTruth.hazardFound: runAgentWorkerOnce submits terminal failures itself, so a naive chain that failed then succeeded would report both outcomes for one task. Fixed and pinned by ROUTE-06.
decisionsRecordedNotAssumed: An uncertain outcome is not retried on another provider unless the caller declares the task idempotent, because the provider may already have done the work. Default is NOT_IDEMPOTENT.

A rejected credential is terminal: a fallback would keep working while the primary credential stayed broken, and trying identities until one is accepted is forbidden behaviour here. Revisitable in one place.
An unrecognised failure class is terminal, because failing over on a failure nobody understands turns one broken call into a bill on every provider.
